extracted.intended_audience: Virginia residents and other stakeholders who want to understand and participate in the state regulatory (notice-and-comment) process
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for how citizens can follow, comment on, petition, and speak about state agency regulations in Virginia, using the Virginia Register and the Virginia Regulatory Town Hall. Includes practical steps for submitting comments, petitioning for rulemaking, and preparing oral testimony at public hearings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the Virginia Register to track regulatory activity
rubrics_metrics.description: The Virginia Register of Regulations is the official biweekly publication of regulations being created, amended, or repealed; all regulations must be filed with the Registrar to become law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Register includes notices of agencies considering changes, proposed changes, emergency regulations, and final adopted regulations. Use it to follow a regulation's progress, find what changes are proposed, where a public hearing will be held, and who to contact to ask questions or submit comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sign up at the Virginia Regulatory Town Hall for notifications
rubrics_metrics.description: The Virginia Regulatory Town Hall is a website (townhall.virginia.gov) where executive branch agencies submit regulations for review and where the public can sign up for email notifications of regulatory activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Town Hall is managed by the Department of Planning and Budget and is a resource for tracking progress and receiving notices of meetings and hearings. NOTE: not all state agencies' regulations are posted on the Town Hall.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post comments using public comment forums (Town Hall)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the Town Hall public comment forum to post written comments regarding specific regulatory actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public comment forums allow stakeholders to submit views on proposed regulations; combine this with direct agency contact if appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact the responsible agency directly
rubrics_metrics.description: Express support or concerns about a regulation by contacting the agency responsible for the regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Virginia Register provides contact information for each printed regulation. Direct contact can supplement forum comments and may help clarify questions or influence agency understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition an agency to promulgate or amend a regulation (petition for rulemaking)
rubrics_metrics.description: You may request that an agency develop a new regulation or amend an existing one by submitting a written petition for rulemaking under § 2.2-4007 A of the Code of Virginia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the agency has statutory authority from the General Assembly to write the regulation. Include your name; the regulation number (if known); and the substance and purpose of the requested rulemaking. The agency is required to provide a written response to your petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confirm agency authority before petitioning
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency can only promulgate or change regulations if the General Assembly has authorized or mandated that agency to do so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before requesting a new regulation or amendment, check whether the enabling statute grants the agency the authority to adopt the requested regulation; petitions outside an agency's authority are unlikely to proceed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare for public hearings by observing format and time limits
rubrics_metrics.description: If possible, attend a public hearing beforehand to understand the hearing format; hearings may limit individual speaking time to ensure everyone can be heard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize your oral remarks: begin by identifying yourself (include credentials and organization if appropriate); clearly state your position; present two to three key points; and support them with appropriate facts. Being concise and organized increases the chance your points will be heard within time limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: If you cannot attend a hearing, use online resources to obtain agendas and minutes
rubrics_metrics.description: Find meeting and hearing information (agenda, minutes) through the Commonwealth Calendar and the Virginia Regulatory Town Hall.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public hearings on regulations are also published with the proposed regulation in the Virginia Register. Use these resources to follow proceedings and to submit written comments if you cannot attend in person.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use multiple channels to increase impact (Register, Town Hall, direct contact)
rubrics_metrics.description: Combine use of the Virginia Register, Town Hall notifications/forums, and direct agency contact to monitor and influence regulatory action effectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each resource has different strengths: the Register is the official publication and shows formal filings/hearings; Town Hall offers tracking and comment forums plus email alerts; direct agency contact provides personalized communication. Relying on multiple channels helps ensure your participation is received and recorded.
